clue.text: It's designed to help you see pale daffodil

definitions.text: It's designed to help you see

parts.note: pale colours are light ones
a daffodil grows from a bulb, so the plant stands for its bulb

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a pale daffodil bred to brighten the view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daffodil' gives BULB by naming the plant for the thing it grows from.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp's glass globe exists to provide illumination so people can see in the dark.

clue.text: Very many cargoes

definitions.meaning: freight carried by a vehicle or ship

explanation.definitionFit: A great quantity is lots, and a lorry's freight is its burden; the same word covers both.

clue.text: Balk at charges, and enter uninvited

definitions.meaning: refuse to pay the admission fee by sneaking in
turn up at a party without an invitation

explanation.definitionFit: Slipping into a party or event without a ticket both dodges the fee and arrives unasked.

clue.text: One of two presents later this month

definitions.text: One of two presents later this month

parts.words: One of two presents later this month
parts.note: in the carol of Christmas gifts, the second day brings a pair of birds; this puzzle ran in December

explanation.surface: Someone planning gifts for later in the month.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' has 'two turtle doves' on the second day.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is one of the pair given on the second day of the carol's Christmas.

clue.text: Sudden rush increases desire

parts.note: ups are rises or increases
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A surge of feeling makes a craving grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden increase or rush of something.

clue.text: Looked through lines in plot

indicators.note: in puts the lines inside the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
rows are lines

explanation.surface: Someone scanned the lines of a story's plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a story, but here it is a flower BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to skim or look casually through something.

clue.text: Man whose account 25 features in a book of the Bible

indicators.note: something that features in another appears inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A biblical man whose story is told in one of the scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features in' puts AC inside JOB. The '25' in the clue as held is a stray printing mark and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: The patriarch Jacob, son of Isaac, is a male figure of Genesis.

clue.text: Precious stone is almost exhausted

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: jaded means worn out

explanation.surface: A gemstone that has nearly run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Jade is a green ornamental gem.

clue.text: Cabbage served with unknown fish

parts.note: cole is an old word for cabbage, as in coleslaw
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A dinner of cabbage served with some unidentified fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Coley is an edible sea fish of the cod family, also called saithe.

clue.text: Lover could be fiery when limited by tie

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in on both sides by the tie

parts.note: a bond is a tie

indicators.note: could be signals the letters of fiery may take another form

explanation.surface: A passionate partner could turn hot-headed when constrained by commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges FIERY to YFRIE, which 'limited by' puts inside BOND.
explanation.definitionFit: A man someone is romantically attached to is their partner or sweetheart.

clue.text: Looking for dessert which is not finished

indicators.note: a word that is not finished loses its last letter, here the closing S

parts.note: afters is British slang for the pudding course

explanation.surface: Someone on the hunt for a pudding they never got to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is everyday British for the pudding course; 'which is not finished' drops its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after something is to be seeking or pursuing it.

clue.text: In which contestant must foil his opponent?

definitions.text: In which contestant must foil his opponent?

parts.words: In which contestant must foil his opponent?
parts.note: to foil is to thwart, but a foil is also the blunt fencing blade, so the contest is fencing

explanation.surface: A question about a game where each player tries to thwart the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing is the sport of blade combat, and a foil is one of its weapons.

clue.text: Remove religious content — new clues come up

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of clues are formed into a fresh order

parts.note: to arise is to come up, as a question does

explanation.surface: A puzzle editor strips out the churchy material because new clues have come up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns CLUES into SECUL, then ARISE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something lay is to take away its church or spiritual character.

clue.text: One changing colour of Lady Ermintrude

indicators.note: the letters come out of the words Lady Ermintrude, running across the space

explanation.surface: An aristocratic lady whose complexion keeps shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' takes the run from ladY ERmintrude.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dyes cloth alters its hue for a living.

clue.text: Flo's action developed a method of teaching music

indicators.note: developed suggests letters worked up into something new

parts.note: the name and its s both supply letters

explanation.surface: A woman's initiative grew into a way of teaching music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges FLOS and ACTION. Tonic sol-fa is the doh-ray-me system of naming notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa is a system of sight-singing using syllables for the notes of the scale.

clue.text: Tango with swaying gait? Nonsense

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a waddle is a rocking, side-to-side walk like a duck's

explanation.surface: A dancer's wobbly tango is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, empty talk.

clue.text: After medication wife leaves to take steps to acquire social skill

parts.note: a tablet is a dose of medicine

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: to walk is to take steps

explanation.surface: After taking pills, a woman walks out to learn how to mix with people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes W from WALK, giving ALK.
explanation.definitionFit: Table talk is easy conversation over a meal, a sociable accomplishment.

clue.text: Take chance about negative censorship

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to dice, as in dice with death, is to gamble
not is the word that makes a statement negative

explanation.surface: A gambler bets against a ban on publication.
explanation.walkthrough: A D-NOTICE is a British government request to the press not to publish material on security grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The notice is an official request that keeps sensitive defence stories out of the news.

clue.text: Wild eglantine is not chic

indicators.note: wild suggests letters running out of order

explanation.surface: A rambling wild rose is hardly fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Eglantine is sweet-briar, a wild rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking grace or style is unfashionable and clumsy.

clue.text: Carried on as one with possessions in place of 4 rest

indicators.note: in places the possessor inside the place of rest

parts.note: a bed is where you rest
the haves are people with plenty, so one of them is a have

explanation.surface: Someone with property continued as before in their resting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; the '4' in the clue as held is a stray printing mark and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to conduct oneself, to act or carry on in a certain way.

clue.text: Rubbish, mostly, at one new type of cinema

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: drivel is nonsense
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A new cinema shows mostly rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in is a cinema where the audience watches from parked cars.

clue.text: Dispatch includes gratuity 5 and wage

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to dispatch is to send
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: A payslip sent with a tip added to the pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The '5' in the clue as held is a stray printing mark and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary, as paid to clergy.

clue.text: Salesmen turned up clutching beam disperser

indicators.note: clutching means holding something inside
turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Salesmen arrive grasping a device that sprays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads REPS backwards as SPER, and 'clutching' puts RAY inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprayer scatters liquid in fine droplets.

clue.text: Coin found in old French

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Coin found in old French' (4): no wordplay found that gives EURO from these words; likely garbled by OCR, and no reprint located

clue.text: Shaky description of notes with heavy beat

definitions.text: description of notes with heavy beat
definitions.meaning: music in the style of rock and roll

explanation.definitionFit: The word means unstable, and also describes music with a pounding rock rhythm.

clue.text: What's shown by a bit of sarcasm?

definitions.text: What's shown by a bit of sarcasm?

parts.words: What's shown by a bit of sarcasm?
parts.note: a sarcastic remark shows a lack of regard for its target

explanation.surface: A question about what a sarcastic jibe reveals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm mocks, and so expresses contempt or lack of esteem.

clue.text: Statutory disclosure — one could be instructive

indicators.note: a disclosure reveals what lies inside, here in the word Statutory

explanation.surface: A legal disclosure might prove educational.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher is someone whose job is to instruct.

clue.text: Wake confused, without any energy

indicators.note: confused signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Waking up groggy and drained.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble means lacking strength or energy.

clue.text: One who hates bridge?

parts.note: read as an ..., a foe of arches, the bridging structures, but it also means a chief foe

explanation.surface: A question about someone who loathes the card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game, but it is an arch; the playful reading is a foe of arches.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal foe is someone who detests you above all others.

clue.text: Was dependent, having a far from profitable time?

parts.note: a lean period is one with little profit

explanation.surface: Someone relied on others during a hard spell with no earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: To have relied on someone is to have rested one's weight on them.

clue.text: Reversible canoe

indicators.note: a reversible word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A canoe that can be paddled either way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a covered canoe of Inuit origin.

clue.text: A snorter blowing across Spain?

indicators.note: across means the shuffled letters span the other piece, holding it inside
blowing suggests letters scattered by the wind into a new arrangement

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A powerful gale sweeps over the Iberian peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' rearranges A SNORTER around E. The whole clue is also the definition: a snorter is a violent gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale from the northeast is a strong wind such as might sweep the country.
